skill.name: agent-tool-builder
skill.description: Guidance for designing reliable AI agent tools, including JSON Schema descriptions, examples, validation gates, MCP patterns, error handling, and parallel execution.
skill.summary: Design reliable AI agent tools with clear schemas, validation, MCP patterns, and useful errors.

content.value_statement: Poor tool schemas cause AI agents to call tools incorrectly or fail without useful recovery paths. This skill teaches schema design, validation, MCP patterns, and error handling for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to write clear JSON Schema descriptions for agent tools.
Shows input examples for complex or format-sensitive tool parameters.
Provides error handling patterns that return actionable tool errors.
Covers MCP server structure and inputSchema requirements.
Describes parallel tool execution patterns for independent calls.
Lists validation checks for tool descriptions, parameters, returns, and external calls.
limitations: It is guidance material, not an executable tool generator.
Example code needs adaptation before production use.
It does not audit a repository automatically.
It does not cover every framework or provider-specific release change.

use_cases.title: New Agent Builder
use_cases.description: Design a first tool schema with clear descriptions, required fields, and validation rules.

use_cases.title: MCP Service Design
use_cases.description: Plan a reusable MCP tool with input schema, error results, and access control considerations.

use_cases.title: Tool Reliability Review
use_cases.description: Review existing function-calling tools for weak descriptions, missing validation, and unclear error responses.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Tool Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tool schema for [task]. Include the tool name, purpose, required inputs, optional inputs, examples, and limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Tool Descriptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tool definition: [paste definition]. Rewrite descriptions so an agent knows when to use it and when to avoid it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: For this agent tool: [tool description], define validation errors, external service errors, business logic errors, and recovery messages.

prompt_templates.title: Design an MCP Tool Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a small MCP tool set for [domain]. Include tool boundaries, input schemas, error behavior, parallel call opportunities, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Request: Design a calendar scheduling tool for an assistant.
output: Tool should require title, start time, and duration.
Attendees can be optional with clear email format guidance.
The description should state when the agent should not use the tool.

output_examples.input: Request: Review a weather tool that returns only Failed on errors.
output: Replace generic failures with validation, not found, rate limit, and internal error categories.
Add recovery messages that suggest corrected locations or retry timing.
Mark error results so the agent can recover instead of treating them as success.

output_examples.input: Request: Plan MCP tools for customer support lookup.
output: Separate customer lookup, ticket search, and ticket update into clear tools.
Require identifiers for write actions and validate them before execution.
Document permissions and error responses for missing or restricted records.

best_practices: Write descriptions that explain when to use a tool and when to avoid it.
Validate all LLM-provided inputs before the implementation touches external systems.
Return clear error messages that help the agent recover or ask the user.
anti_patterns: Using vague tool names or one-sentence descriptions for complex actions.
Returning silent failures or generic errors without recovery guidance.
Building many overlapping tools when one precise tool would be clearer.

faq.question: Does this skill generate tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides design and review. You still implement and test the tool in your own codebase.

faq.question: Which platforms does it mention?
faq.answer: It covers Claude, OpenAI function calling, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, and MCP concepts.

faq.question: Can it help with MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains MCP tool structure, inputSchema requirements, tool results, and reusable tool design.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes input validation, permission errors, parameterized SQL, and timeouts for external calls.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts with schema basics and then moves into error handling, MCP, and parallel execution.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to Codex, Claude Code, and other agent builders that use tool schemas.
